parole.testo: Borrowed from German Archäologie, from Ancient Greek ἀρχαιολογία (arkhaiología, “antiquarian lore, ancient legends, history”), from ἀρχαῖος (arkhaîos, “primal, old, ancient”), with -ло́гія (-lóhija) ending from Ancient Greek -λογία (-logía). Compare Russian археоло́гия (arxeológija), Belarusian архе
Borrowed from German Gen, coined by Danish scientist Wilhelm Johannsen in 1909, from Ancient Greek γένος (génos).

From German Ökologie (coined by Ernst Haeckel), from Ancient Greek οἶκος (oîkos, “house”) + -λογία (-logía, “study of”). By surface analysis, еко- (eko-) + -логія (-lohija). Compare Russian эколо́гия (ekológija), Belarusian экало́гія (ekalóhija), Polish ekologia.
Borrowed from German Enzym, coined 1878 by the German physiologist Wilhelm Kühne from Ancient Greek ἐν (en, “in”) + ζύμη (zúmē, “yeast”).
Borrowed from German Entropie, from Ancient Greek ἐντροπῐ́ᾱ (entropĭ́ā). Compare Russian энтропи́я (entropíja), Belarusian энтрапі́я (entrapíja), Polish entropia.
Borrowed from German Erotik, from Ancient Greek ἐρωτικός (erōtikós). Compare Russian эро́тика (erótika), Belarusian эро́тыка (erótyka), Polish erotyka.

Borrowed from German Morphologie, ultimately from Ancient Greek μορφή (morphḗ, “shape, form”), with -ло́гія (-lóhija) ending from Ancient Greek -λογία (-logía). Compare Russian морфоло́гия (morfológija), Belarusian марфало́гія (marfalóhija), Polish morfologia.
Borrowed from German Parameter, from Ancient Greek παρά (pará, “beside”) + μέτρον (métron, “measure”).
Borrowed from German Polymer, from Ancient Greek πολύς (polús, “many”) + μέρος (méros, “part”). Compare Russian полиме́р (polimér), Belarusian паліме́р (palimjér).
Borrowed from German Polytop. By surface analysis, полі- (poli-, “poly-”) + -топ (-top, “-tope”), from Ancient Greek τόπος (tópos, “region; area”).

Borrowed from German Psychiatrie, from Ancient Greek ψυχή (psukhḗ, “soul, mind”) and ἰατρεία (iatreía, “healing, medical treatment”). Compare Russian психиатри́я (psixiatríja), Belarusian псіхіятры́я (psixijatrýja), Polish psychiatria.
Borrowed from German Pykniker, influenced by the physique typology proposed by German psychiatrist Ernst Kretschmer, from Ancient Greek πυκνός (puknós, “thick, dense”).

parole.significato: pyrotechnics (the art and technology of fireworks and related military applications)
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from German Pyrotechnik, ultimately from Ancient Greek πῦρ (pûr) and τέχνη (tékhnē). Compare Russian пироте́хника (pirotéxnika), Belarusian піратэ́хніка (piratéxnika), Polish pirotechnika.

parole.significato: scepticism, scepsis (UK), skepticism, skepsis (US) (a studied attitude of questioning and doubt)
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from German Skepsis, from Ancient Greek σκέψις (sképsis).
Internationalism originally coined as German Phaenotypus in 1909 (whence Phänotyp), ultimately from Ancient Greek φαίνω (phaínō, “to shine, to show, to appear”) + τύπος (túpos, “mark, type”).

parole.significato: phonetics (branch of linguistics that studies sounds and their representation by written symbols, for example IPA)
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Phonetik, from Ancient Greek φωνητῐκός (phōnētĭkós).
